newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Escelsa eyes power privatizations.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Escelsa eyes power privatizations.

text.p: Just two years after its own privatization, Brazilian electrical firm Escelsa SA plans to take part in further power selloffs, including the upcoming sale of Bahia state's Coelba, said the company's president.
"Escelsa wants to grow. That's why it is interested in other companies," Escelsa chief Francisco Gomide told a conference on the privatization of Brazil's power sector.
"It wants new clients, and the only way to do that is to buy other companies. We will go to all the auctions possible in our area," he added.
Gomide said the company is waiting for the June 6 publication of Coelba's bid specifications before deciding on a partner for the auction.
Gomide also said Escelsa plans to branch out into natural gas, cable TV and fiber optics in order to boost the company's profitability.
He said Escelsa signed an agreement on May 16 with state oil firm Petrobras to develop the offshore Sao Matos gas field as a way to meet growing power demand in its home state of Espirito Santo.
Privatized in 1995, Escelsa has 700,000 customers and expects to grow by five percent or 35,000 clients per year in the coming years.
The company's client base grew 20 percent in the 1994/1995 period and 14 percent in 1995 and 1996.
"We expect growth to be a little slower, between five and seven percent for 1996 and 1997," Gomide said, adding the company's growth rate is faster than the country's.
Escelsa plans to have invested some 250 million reais over a three year period ending at the end of 1998, he said.
He said Escelsa also wants to participate in privatizations of water and sewage companies in order to take advantage of "synergies among utilities."
Gomide said electrical utilities worldwide have a low risk for investors and therefore a relatively low return. By diversifying, Escelsa can give investors a higher return.
